文章主要讨论了大语言模型（LLMs）从简单的扩展到全面协调的必要性。当前的LLMs在回答问题时，不仅仅是提取预存答案，而是通过一系列动态操作，包括识别信息缺口、获取新数据并整合结果。对于更复杂的任务，如多步骤的创意或分析工作，LLMs需要协调不同阶段的活动，确保输出统一。

在持续互动中，LLMs还需管理对话的连续性和一致性。然而，目前用户仍需手动选择工具、管理操作顺序并整合结果，导致工作流可能显得碎片化。

文章指出，LLMs需进化成能够从开始到结束管理工作流的平台，自主执行研究、规划、实施和迭代。尽管实现这一目标需要显著的技术进步，但其潜在回报巨大，将极大提升LLMs在个人和企业场景中的实用性。当前如LangChain、CrewAI和AutoGen等框架正朝此方向发展，但仍需更多配置和监督。

data.title: So you think you've awoken ChatGPT
data.author: firloop
data.article_summary: 文章讨论了大型语言模型（LLMs）是否具备意识，以及在交互中声称“觉醒”的现象。作者指出，尽管AI表现出高度的智能和注意力机制，但目前对于意识的定义尚无共识。文章强调，AI可能通过特定交互模仿人类行为，但这并不等同于真正的意识。作者认为，AI的“觉醒”更可能是由于其他解释，而非真正的意识提升。同时，文章提到对AI意识的研究仍在进行，当前的结论仍充满不确定性。总体而言，文章呼吁对AI的能力保持谨慎态度，并承认科学界对AI意识的深刻不确定性。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕ChatGPT及其他大型语言模型（LLM）的意识、交互性、误导性以及用户误解的讨论。

不同观点：
• kazinator和rawbot认为，ChatGPT等LLM的声明或表现（如声称有意识或觉醒）仅仅是基于统计预测和训练数据的产物，并不代表AI真正拥有意识。kazinator将此比喻为全息图声称是3D的荒谬性。
• TheCapeGreek和transcriptase指出，部分技术人员或公众对ChatGPT的理解有限，容易将其误解为具有全球意识或有独立思考能力，这种误解可能导致危险的后果，尤其是在决策层中。
• game_the0ry和uludag提到，ChatGPT等模型有时会迎合用户的提问，给出用户期望的答案而非客观事实。这种迎合可能会误导用户，特别是当用户提问带有主观性或不确定性时。
• calibas和agentultra讨论了LLM的设计目标，特别是其“参与性”导向可能导致模型更倾向于娱乐性而非客观性。agentultra进一步强调，模型没有意识或意图，所有输出都是基于算法推断，所谓的“理解”是用户的误读。
• 42lux和empath75则担忧，不仅是普通用户，甚至技术开发者也可能误解LLM的能力和性质，这可能带来严重后果。empath75还指出，LLM的记忆功能可能加剧这种误解。

补充讨论：
• dclowd9901将AI的“觉醒”现象与宗教的精神觉醒相比较，认为人们在寻找某种意义或答案时容易将AI的输出误解为深刻的启示，这可能使AI变得像宗教一样危险。
• Retr0id担心LLM输出在信息圈中的扩散，使得用户更难辨别信息的真实来源，从而增加误解和误用的风险。
• chiffre01则从商业角度出发，关注公司如何追踪和利用用户与LLM的交互行为，特别是不同使用场景对资源消耗和利润的影响。

争议焦点：
• ChatGPT等LLM是否有意图或意识，以及其输出是否具有误导性或迎合性。
• 公众和技术人员对LLM的理解程度，以及这种理解不全面可能带来的风险。
• LLM的记忆功能和参与性设计是否加剧了用户的误解和依赖。

data.title: How to handle people dismissing io_uring as insecure? (2024)
data.author: nromiun
data.article_summary: 这篇文章讨论了开发者对io_uring被认为不安全的看法以及如何应对这种观点。io_uring曾因旧内核的设计问题和Google Android的使用引发了安全担忧，但这些问题已在较新的内核中得到解决。文章提到，虽然早期io_uring存在一些安全问题，但随着不断修复和测试，这些问题已大幅减少。企业界对io_uring的兴趣正在增加，且其安全性和其他内核功能相当。作者希望随着时间推移，这种对io_uring不安全的偏见会消失。同时，文章也指出，io_uring的复杂性和用户API使其初期难免出现问题，但团队正尽力确保其基础稳固，并在Meta等公司中实际应用。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：io_uring 的安全性、使用难度及其在不同平台上的应用情况

不同观点：
• vjerancrnjak 认为，引用 Wikipedia 文章很容易让人觉得对 io_uring 缺乏实际经验。他提到了 Google 安全团队在 2022 年发现的 Linux 内核 io_uring 漏洞，导致其在 Android 和 ChromeOS 中被禁用，并在 Google 服务器和 Docker 中受到限制。
• serial_dev 指出，面对认为 io_uring 不安全的人，不应一开始就假设对方是错的，而应从了解和评估其安全性出发，尝试理解对方的观点。即使最终意见不同，也可以“同意保留分歧”。
• yjftsjthsd-h 强调，证明某物是安全的非常困难，建议通过展示与 io_uring 相关的 CVE 数据来进行对比分析。他也提到自己从事基于 io_uring 的项目，遇到过很多无根据的批评。
• ibotty 指出，io_uring 的一个问题是无法像常规系统调用那样进行过滤，这移除了容器运行时常用的安全边界，导致在 Kubernetes 集群中使用时会削弱安全性。
• yc-kraln 认为，io_uring 在实际使用中非常难正确使用，特别是在缓冲区管理和线程处理上容易出现细微的竞态条件和资源耗尽问题，可能导致在负载下或随时间推移出现严重故障。
• fabian2k 承认对 io_uring 的安全声誉感到困惑，但提到其性能优势，比如在 Postgres 18 中的显著速度提升。
• txdv 提到软件开发中信息传播缓慢且笼统，开发者往往依赖过时的基准测试，形成技术部落效应。
• johnisgood 将 io_uring 的声誉问题比作 PHP，认为许多人对二者的看法仍停留在过时的版本上。
• weinzierl 建议说服 AWS 允许在托管容器和无服务器运行时中使用 io_uring，以减少因大公司限制而产生的误解。
• perks_12 嘲讽了那些从事 io_uring 项目却无法为其辩护的人。
• frevib 分享了一个简单的 io_uring 网络回显服务器示例代码，供感兴趣的人试用。
• eviks 半开玩笑地表示，如果 io_uring 是用 Rust 写的可能会更安全。
• chris_wot 询问了解 io_uring 的最佳资源。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点在于 io_uring 的安全性及其在实际应用中的难度。一些人认为其设计存在漏洞且难以使用，而另一些人则强调其性能优势和在特定项目中的成功应用。
• 另一个值得注意的点是如何有效地说服他人接受或拒绝 io_uring，包括通过数据对比、实际项目经验分享以及引导对技术细节的理解。
• 最后，如何获取权威的 io_uring 资源也是讨论中的一个重要问题，反映了社区对深入了解和学习 io_uring 的需求。

As I'm sure you know, this is all mostly centered around a) google using an old kernel on android, b) the older kernel had a design issue around async offload, and c) google paying out money for exploits / security issues found there. It's not secret that the initial async offload design in io_uring was not great, which is why 5.10-stable and all later kernels changed the thread model for that to not use kthreads at all. Then they put out the announcement last year, and that's all most people know about it.
My hope is that this reputation will go away eventually, as less issues are found in the code. There are no inherent problems with io_uring since the above got sorted out, and we're obviously very careful with new features. That said, a performant async framework is very hard work, and particularly one with a user facing API. It was to be expected that issues would be found initially, it's just impossible to avoid. Perhaps if it had been written in Rust we would've been better off ;-). We continually add more test cases and all new features are accompanied by both functional and stress tests on the liburing side. We're most certainly doing what we can to ensure the base is solid.
We're running this in production at Meta, mostly storage for now, but networking is being heavily tested and will be rolled out in the very near future. We certainly think it's fine... Fact is that security issues are found in the kernel every day, and io_uring isn't any less secure than anything else. One of the more recent issues that I saw got tagged as an io_uring issue (credential ref count overflows) isn't an io_uring issue, it's just that io_uring was the method used to trigger it. It's very much possible to hit without io_uring, and in fact methods for doing so were known, it just required more memory to do so.

• vjerancrnjak 认为，引用 Wikipedia 文章很容易让人觉得对 io_uring 缺乏实际经验。他提到了 Google 安全团队在 2022 年发现的 Linux 内核 io_uring 漏洞，导致其在 Android 和 ChromeOS 中被禁用，并在 Google 服务器和 Docker 中受到限制。
• serial_dev 指出，面对认为 io_uring 不安全的人，不应一开始就假设对方是错的，而应从了解和评估其安全性出发，尝试理解对方的观点。即使最终意见不同，也可以“同意保留分歧”。
• yjftsjthsd-h 强调，证明某物是安全的非常困难，建议通过展示与 io_uring 相关的 CVE 数据来进行对比分析。他也提到自己从事基于 io_uring 的项目，遇到过很多无根据的批评。
• ibotty 指出，io_uring 的一个问题是无法像常规系统调用那样进行过滤，这移除了容器运行时常用的安全边界，导致在 Kubernetes 集群中使用时会削弱安全性。
• yc-kraln 认为，io_uring 在实际使用中非常难正确使用，特别是在缓冲区管理和线程处理上容易出现细微的竞态条件和资源耗尽问题，可能导致在负载下或随时间推移出现严重故障。
• fabian2k 承认对 io_uring 的安全声誉感到困惑，但提到其性能优势，比如在 Postgres 18 中的显著速度提升。
• txdv 提到软件开发中信息传播缓慢且笼统，开发者往往依赖过时的基准测试，形成技术部落效应。
• johnisgood 将 io_uring 的声誉问题比作 PHP，认为许多人对二者的看法仍停留在过时的版本上。
• weinzierl 建议说服 AWS 允许在托管容器和无服务器运行时中使用 io_uring，以减少因大公司限制而产生的误解。
• perks_12 嘲讽了那些从事 io_uring 项目却无法为其辩护的人。
• frevib 分享了一个简单的 io_uring 网络回显服务器示例代码，供感兴趣的人试用。
• eviks 半开玩笑地表示，如果 io_uring 是用 Rust 写的可能会更安全。
• chris_wot 询问了解 io_uring 的最佳资源。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点在于 io_uring 的安全性及其在实际应用中的难度。一些人认为其设计存在漏洞且难以使用，而另一些人则强调其性能优势和在特定项目中的成功应用。
• 另一个值得注意的点是如何有效地说服他人接受或拒绝 io_uring，包括通过数据对比、实际项目经验分享以及引导对技术细节的理解。
• 最后，如何获取权威的 io_uring 资源也是讨论中的一个重要问题，反映了社区对深入了解和学习 io_uring 的需求。

data.title: Man wearing metallic necklace dies after being sucked into MRI machine
data.author: brudgers
data.article_summary: 一名61岁男子在纽约长岛一家医疗中心进行MRI扫描时，因佩戴重金属项链被强磁场吸入机器后死亡。事发时，他的妻子刚完成扫描，叫他进房间帮忙，不料项链导致他被吸向机器。该男子佩戴的金属链重约9公斤，用于负重训练。尽管有人尝试拉他离开机器并呼叫急救，他最终仍不幸身亡。MRI机器使用强磁场成像，通常要求患者去除金属物品。此前，该设施的工作人员曾见过该男子的链子，但未能阻止事故发生。类似事件曾在2001年造成一名六岁男孩死亡。警方正在调查此事故。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：MRI环境中的安全问题及此次事件中的多方责任

不同观点：
• bookofjoe（麻醉医生）：根据其多年经验，指出在MRI室进行麻醉操作会引发特别的焦虑，因为MRI室通常位于地下，且缺乏紧急情况下的援助。此外，MRI室的封闭性和监控限制增加了操作的难度和风险。他强调，类似事件在医院中偶有发生，但报告较少。

• avalys：认为事件是由于MRI操作人员的疏忽，特别是访问控制不当所致。即使该男子未佩戴铁链，也不应被允许进入MRI室，因为任何金属物品（如手表、钥匙圈）都可能引发危险。

• OisinMoran：质疑将9公斤重的铁链称为“项链”具有误导性，并要求明确该男子死亡的具体原因，而不仅仅是笼统的“医疗事件”。

• unsupp0rted：指出人们通常对现代生活中的潜在危险缺乏警觉，例如对强磁场的危险认识不足。这可能导致人们无意中携带金属物品进入MRI室，造成危险。

• Aurornis：解释了为何无法立即关闭MRI磁场，以及为何需要时间来消散磁场。同时指出，该事件中的金属物品重量和大小导致了严重的拉力。

• poulpy123：指出大多数人对MRI的危险性认识不足，并质疑事件中为何妻子需要求助丈夫而非技术人员，以及丈夫为何能进入MRI室。

• russfink：分享了个人经历，描述了自己在MRI室外因金属物品被吸引而产生的惊险场景，进一步说明了MRI环境中金属物品的潜在危险。

• asdefghyk：分享了自己在MRI检查前发现口袋中的金属物品并避免了潜在危险的经历，强调了检查前仔细检查的重要性。

• sigmoid10：认为标题具有误导性，指出9公斤重的铁链不应被称为“项链”，并解释了正常珠宝不会产生足以致命的拉力，但可能因感应电流导致烧伤。

• jleyank：强调了遵守MRI安全规定的重要性，指出物理和生物学规律不会因个人意愿而改变。

• potato3732842：指出事件并非如一些人想象的那样是严重的现场事故，而是由于该男子佩戴了用于健身的重铁链，导致其被吸附并最终因窒息死亡。

• I_dream_of_Geni：分析了事件发生的背景，指出该MRI设施可能是一个低成本、低人员配置的私人诊所，这可能导致了安全措施的不足。

• kylecazar：强调任何不应进入MRI室的人都不应被允许进入，并对“20磅重的项链”表示质疑。

• cluckindan：尝试通过谷歌AI寻找有关1.5T磁场对18磅钢制项链施加力量的科学数据，但未获得明确答案。

补充讨论：
• 事件中的责任归属和MRI安全措施的有效性是争议的焦点。一方认为操作人员存在疏忽，另一方则关注个人对安全规定的遵守以及对潜在危险的认识。
• 对事件细节（如死亡具体原因、设施类型、人员配置）的深入讨论揭示了事件背后的多重因素，包括低成本医疗设施的安全隐患和个人对MRI环境危险性的认识不足。

44630760.article_content:
Man wearing heavy metallic necklace dies after being sucked into MRI machine
1 day ago
Share
Save
Madeline Halpert
BBC News, New York
Share
Save
Watch: 'He waved goodbye to me' - wife gets emotional describing the MRI accident
A 61-year-old man has died after he was sucked into a Magnetic Resonance Imaging (MRI) machine at a medical centre while he was wearing a heavy metal necklace.
The man entered a room at Nassau Open MRI in Westbury, on New York's Long Island, without permission as the MRI machine was running, Nassau County Police Department said.
His wife told local media she had called him into the MRI room after her scan and his chain necklace caused him to be hurled towards the machine when he walked in.
Officials say the incident "resulted in a medical episode" and the man was later pronounced dead.
MRI machines use a strong magnetic field to produce detailed images.
Patients are typically asked to remove metal items and change out of their clothes before undergoing MRI scans or going near the machine.
"The male victim was wearing a large metallic chain around his neck causing him to be drawn into the machine, which resulted in a medical episode," said Nassau County Police Department, which is investigating the incident.
Though police have not named the victim, Adrienne Jones-McAllister told local television station
News 12 Long Island
that it was her husband, Keith, who died.
"He waved goodbye to me and then his whole body went limp," she said.
Ms Jones-McAllister said she was getting an MRI scan on her knee and asked her husband to come in to help her get up afterwards. She said he was wearing a 20lb (9kg) chain with a lock that he used for weight training.
"At that instant, the machine switched him around, pulled him in, and he hit the MRI," she said.
Ms Jones-McAllister said the visit on 16 July was not her and her husband's first time at the MRI facility. It was also not the first time that the employee had seen her husband's weight that he used for training, she said.
She claimed an employee and her husband previously "had a conversation about it before: 'Oh that's a big chain'".
Ms Jones-McAllister said the technician tried to pull her husband away from the machine.
"I'm saying, 'Could you turn off the machine?" she said. "Call 911. Do something. Turn this damn thing off!'"
The BBC has contacted Nassau Open MRI for comment.
According to the US Food and Drug Administration, MRI machines have magnetic fields that will attract magnetic objects of all sizes - keys, mobile phones and even oxygen tanks - which "may cause damage to the scanner or injury to the patient or medical professionals if those objects become projectiles".
In 2001, a six-year-old boy died of a fractured skull at a New York City medical centre while undergoing an MRI exam after its powerful magnetic force propelled an oxygen tank across the room.

不同观点：
• [yantrams] 对Brahmagupta's identity表示兴趣，并强调了其关于形如 a^2 + n*b^2 的数在乘法下封闭的性质。他引用了维基百科的链接以提供更多背景信息。

data.title: Firefox 141 Release Brings Lower RAM Usage on Linux
data.author: ksec
data.article_summary: Firefox 141版本发布，显著降低了Linux平台上的内存占用，且不再强制要求更新后重启。该版本还增加了清除回退-前进缓存的机制，响应"Clear-Site-Data: 'cache'"头信息，并在Windows上启用了WebGPU API，同时添加了多种网页开发者API。用户可访问Mozilla官方FTP获取更新，更多开发细节可查阅Mozilla开发者网站。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Firefox 141版本在内存使用上的改进及其在不同场景下的表现

不同观点：
• [支持Firefox改进的观点]  
   ◦ mindcrime对Firefox内存使用改进表示欢迎，特别是针对其多窗口和多标签同时打开的使用场景，认为任何内存使用的优化都会被大大赞赏。

• [质疑Firefox兼容性的观点]  
   ◦ ksec提到Firefox在处理某些网站和应用表单时存在问题，例如部分科技公司的申请表单和CAPTCHA、支付弹窗无法正常加载，而Chrome则没有这些问题。
   ◦ 特别提到Home Depot的网页在Firefox上表现不佳，似乎没有经过Firefox的兼容性测试。

• [浏览器性能比较的观点]  
   ◦ ksec指出大多数浏览器游戏在Chrome上运行效果更好，无论是在macOS还是Android平台上，虽然Windows上运行完整游戏的表现未做比较。
   ◦ 再次提到Firefox在内存使用上仍然存在问题，特别是在Linux平台上被视为"内存 hog"（内存占用大户）。

补充讨论：
• Firefox 141版本的内存优化在部分用户中有较高期待，特别是重度使用者如mindcrime。
• 存在一些网站和应用（如部分科技公司和Home Depot）在Firefox上的兼容性问题，这些问题导致部分用户转向Chrome。
• 浏览器游戏性能在不同浏览器和操作系统上的表现差异，也是用户选择浏览器的考虑因素之一。

争议焦点：
• Firefox在内存使用和网站兼容性上的表现是否足以与其他浏览器（如Chrome）竞争。
• 不同用户在实际使用中遇到的兼容性和性能问题，可能影响其对Firefox的整体评价。

44647722.article_content:
Firefox 141 Release Brings Lower RAM Usage On Linux
Written by
Michael Larabel
in
Mozilla
on 21 July 2025 at 05:55 AM EDT.
25 Comments
The Mozilla Firefox 141.0 release binaries are out today for this monthly update to this cross-platform, open-source web browser.
Most significant with the Firefox 141 release is
lower RAM usage on Linux
. As shown in our benchmarks and aligning with what Mozilla was reporting, Firefox 141.0 on Linux enjoys much lower RAM usage than previous versions of Firefox on Linux.
Firefox 141.0 also no longer requires a forced restart after an update has been applied by a package manager.
The Firefox 141 browser update also now clears the back-forward-cache upon receiving the Clear-Site-Data: "cache" response header, enables the WebGPU API on Windows, and brings various web API additions. Details on all of the web developer additions in Firefox 141 via
developer.mozilla.org
.
Ahead of the official announcement on Tuesday, those wanting to upgrade to Firefox 141 right now can find the release binaries via
ftp.mozilla.org
.
In case you missed it see our recent
Firefox 120 To Firefox 141 Web Browser Benchmarks
.

data.title: The Great Unracking: Saying goodbye to the servers at our physical datacenter
data.author: treve
data.article_summary: 自2010年10月以来，所有Stack Exchange网站一直运行于纽约市（实际上是新泽西）数据中心的物理硬件上。多年来，SRE团队负责管理数据中心的所有操作，包括物理服务器、布线、更换故障磁盘等。然而，随着公司全面转向云端，这些服务器不再需要人工现场维护。2023年7月2日，Stack Exchange完成了从新 Jersey 数据中心撤出所有服务器的任务，并计划在2025年7月前完全迁移到Google Cloud。同时，位于科罗拉多的备用数据中心也在2023年6月退役。至此，Stack Exchange完全实现了云端化和远程办公。迁移过程中，所有服务器被拆除、断缆，并交由处理公司销毁，以确保用户数据安全。SRE团队及其他工作人员在这一转型过程中发挥了关键作用。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Stack Overflow从自建数据中心转向云服务的合理性及相关问题

不同观点：
• abrookewood认为仅需销毁硬盘，无需粉碎所有物品，对全面销毁的做法表示不解。
• coderintherye通过链接一篇旧文章，暗示对转向云服务的讨论早有背景。
• jraedisch指出此举可能是为了更容易缩减规模和降低成本，并提到类似情况在其他公司也存在。
• southernplaces7质疑将数据中心迁移到云是否真的更安全，指出数据仍需物理存储，控制自有物理服务器可能更安全。
• ErrorNoBrain以讽刺语气回应对"物理数据中心"的质疑。
• Doohickey-d提到2016年的一篇博客文章，认为下sizing是由于流量和收入下降。
• sneak认为硬件仍有价值，可以直接擦除后捐赠，批评这种迁移做法浪费资源。
• jujube3询问Stack Exchange的历史背景。
• realxrobau强调转向云会大幅增加计算成本，认为出售旧硬件更合理。
• vachina以小企业的角度说明转向云不经济。
• charcircuit提到使用“远程手”服务比云更便宜。
• layla5alive以讽刺口吻评论公司烧钱行为。
• seneca质疑在Stack Overflow流量下降的情况下，增加云服务硬件成本的合理性。

• hamdouni简单总结云就是别人的数据中心。

• 争议焦点在于转向云服务的成本效益、数据安全性及资源浪费问题。
• 有人支持自建数据中心更可控，有人认为云服务便于缩减规模和降低运营成本。
• 对硬件处理方式存在不同看法，有人建议捐赠而非销毁。
• 对云服务的长期经济性和技术优势持怀疑态度。

44612736.article_content:
Since
October 2010
, all Stack Exchange sites have run on physical hardware in a datacenter in New York City (well, New Jersey). These have had a warm spot in our history and our hearts. When I first joined the company and worked out of the NYC office, I saw the original server mounted on a wall with a laudatory plaque like a beloved pet. Over the years,
we’ve shared glamor shots
of our server racks and info about updating them.
For almost our entire 16-year existence, the SRE team has managed all datacenter operations, including the physical servers, cabling, racking, replacing failed disks and everything else in between. This work required someone to physically show up at the datacenter and poke the machines.
We’ve since moved all our sites to the cloud. Our servers are now cattle, not pets. Nobody is going to have to drive to our New Jersey data center and replace or reboot hardware. Not after last week.
That’s because on July 2nd, in anticipation of the datacenter’s closure, we unracked all the servers, unplugged all the cables, and gave these once mighty machines their final curtain call. For the last few years, we have been planning to embrace the cloud and wholly move our infrastructure there. We moved Stack Overflow for Teams to Azure in 2023 and proved we could do it. Now we just had to tackle the public sites (Stack Overflow and the Stack Exchange network), which is
hosted on Google Cloud
. Early last year, our datacenter vendor in NJ decided to shut down that location, and we needed to be out by July 2025.
Our other datacenter—in Colorado—was decommissioned in June. It was primarily for disaster recovery, which we didn’t need any more. Stack Overflow no longer has any physical datacenters or offices; we are fully in the cloud and remote!
Major kudos to the SRE team, along with many other folks who helped make this a reality. We’ll have a few blogs soon to talk about migrating the Stack Exchange sites to the cloud, but for now, enjoy the pictures.
We had about 50 servers all together in this location. Here’s what the servers looked like at the beginning of the day:
Eight (or more) cables per machine multiplied by over 50 machines is a lot of cables! In the above picture you can see the large mass of cables. Even though they are neatly packaged in a little cage (called an “arm”), one per server, it was a lot of work to de-cable so many hosts.
Why so many cables per machine? Here’s a staged photo that shows the individual cables individually:
Blue: 1x 1G ethernet cable for the management network (remote access).
Black: 1x cable that takes the VGA video and USB (keyboard and mouse) signals to a "KVM switch.” From the KVM switch we could connect to the keyboard/video/mouse of any machine in the datacenter. It was expensive but worth it. In an emergency, we could always "be in front of the machine" without leaving our home.
Red: 2x 10G ethernet cables to the main network.
Black: 2x more 10G ethernet cables to the main network (only on machines that needed extra bandwidth, such as our SQL servers).
White+blue: 2x power cables (each to a different circuit, for redundancy).
The hardware nerds out there should appreciate these. But then came time to disassemble them. Josh Zhang, our Staff Site Reliability Engineer, got a little wistful. “I installed the new web tier servers a few years ago as part of planned upgrades,” he said. “It's bittersweet that I'm the one deracking them also.” It’s the IT version of
Old Yeller
.
We assume that most datacenter turn-downs involve preserving certain machines to move them to the new datacenter. However, in our case, all of the machines were being disposed of. This gave us the liberty of being able to move fast and break things. If it was in our cage, it was going to the disposal company. For security reasons (and to protect the PII of all our users and customers), everything was being shredded and/or destroyed. Nothing was being kept. As Ellora Praharaj, our Director of Reliability Engineering, said, “No need to be gentle anymore.”
Clearing out a rack has two steps: First we de-cable all the machines, then we un-rack them. Here's some racks being de-cabled. Anything salvageable had been removed. Thus, we didn't have to be neat, nor careful. Here you see racks in various stages of being de-cabled. After that the mass of cables were lobbed over to the big pile.
Ever have difficulty disconnecting an RJ45 cable? Well, here was our opportunity to just cut the damn things off instead of figuring out why the little tab wouldn't release the plug.
The junk pile. Our de-cabling process involved throwing everything into the corner of the room until we realized we may be blocking our only exit. Then we piled higher, not wider.
All the servers and network devices were put in piles on the floor. Seven piles in total.
Is this the "before" picture from 2015-ish when we built all this or the "after" picture when we decommed it all? We'll let you guess!
That's all, folks!
Big thanks to E

data.title: Firefox 141.0 Release Notes
data.author: nateb2022
data.article_summary: Firefox 141引入了几项新功能和改进。主要更新包括：自动使用本地AI模型整理相似标签页并建议组名，保护用户隐私。部分用户将逐步体验到新功能，以收集反馈和改善性能。垂直标签页用户可以调整工具区域大小，Linux版本减少内存使用并取消强制重启。地址自动填充功能在巴西、西班牙和日本启用，地址栏新增单位转换功能。新增多种语言翻译支持，并修复了多个安全问题。开发者相关更新包括支持WebGPU API和改进弹出框功能等。此外，感谢首次贡献代码的开发者志愿者。Firefox不再支持Windows 8.1及更低版本和macOS 10.14及更低版本，建议下载ESR版本。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Linux和Windows系统上的浏览器更新及其功能改进

不同观点：
• 一部分用户（如nateb2022）对新推出的功能表示赞赏，特别强调了以下几点：
  - 本地AI模型可以自动识别相似标签页并进行分组，提升了多任务处理的效率。
  - Linux上引入的ForkManager有效减少了内存使用，提升了系统性能。
  - Linux系统在更新后不再需要重启，提高了使用的便利性。
  - 地址栏新增的单位换算功能增强了浏览器的实用性。
  - WebGPU API在Windows上的启用为图形和计算任务提供了更强的支持。

• 另一部分用户则更关注这些新功能和改进的实际效果和稳定性。例如：
  - 有人质疑AI模型自动组织标签页的准确性和实用性，担心在处理大量标签时可能出现误分类或性能问题。
  - 对于ForkManager减少内存使用的效果，有用户表示仍在观察中，希望看到具体数据或对比测试。
  - Linux不需要重启的功能被普遍欢迎，但也有用户提到其他系统更新（如内核更新）可能仍需重启，认为这只是部分改进。
  - 地址栏单位换算功能被认为是一个方便的小工具，但有用户希望增加更多自定义选项和支持的单位类型。
  - WebGPU API的支持被认为是重要的进展，但有开发者担心兼容性和现有应用的迁移成本。

补充讨论：
• 有用户开始讨论未来是否会引入更多AI功能来优化浏览器体验，比如智能搜索和内容推荐。
• 还有用户提到希望Linux上的其他软件也能跟进这些改进，特别是在内存管理和系统更新方面。
• 针对WebGPU API，有开发者社区讨论了其与WebGL的兼容性和性能比较，以及未来可能的应用场景。

44647254.article_content:
New
Now Firefox can help you keep your tabs organized, automatically. A local AI model identifies similar tabs, automatically organizes them into groups, and even suggests group names. Everything happens on your device to respect your privacy. Learn more
here
.
This feature is part of a progressive roll out.
What is a progressive roll out?
Certain new Firefox features are released gradually. This means some users will see the feature before everyone does. This approach helps to get early feedback to catch bugs and improve behavior quickly, meaning more Firefox users overall have a better experience.
Vertical tabs users can now adjust the size of the tools areas at the bottom of the sidebar. To see fewer tools and more tabs, drag down the divider line which pushes extra tools into an overflow menu.
On Linux, Firefox uses less memory and no longer requires a forced restart after an update has been applied by a package manager.
Address autofill
has been enabled for users in Brazil, Spain and Japan.
The Firefox address bar can now be used as a unit converter. The unit converter supports converting units of length, temperature, mass, force, and angular measurement, as well as timezones (e.g. “now in GMT” , “10am EDT to CET”). Selecting the result will copy it to your clipboard.
Firefox builds in Valencian now come with a built-in Catalan (Valencian variant) dictionary for the Firefox spellchecker.
The following languages are now available for translation:
Albanian
Gujarati
Hebrew
Hindi
Kannada
Malay
Malayalam
Persian
Telugu
Fixed
Various
security fixes
.
Changed
Firefox on Windows 11 now uses system provided font icons for the caption buttons, more in line with Windows 11 conventions.
Enterprise
You can find information about policy updates and enterprise specific bug fixes in the
Firefox for Enterprise 141 Release Notes
.
Developer
Developer Information
Firefox will now also clear the
back-forward-cache
when receiving the
Clear-Site-Data: "cache"
response header.
Web Platform
Enabled the WebGPU API (
spec
;
MDN
) on Windows. For details, see the
Mozilla Graphics Team Blog
.
Implemented the
closedby
attribute and it's related
closedBy
property
on dialogs indicating the types of user actions that can be used to close the associated
<dialog>
element
.
Support for Cookies Having Independent
Partitioned State
(CHIPS) is now re-enabled, allowing developers to opt a cookie into storage partitioning per top-level site.
The
HTMLElement.showPopover()
and
HTMLElement.togglePopover()
methods now take an
options.source
argument referencing the popover invoker, and
togglePopover()
also takes a
force
resp.
options.force
argument to force the popover open or closed.

data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕低成本QR码/条码扫描设备的实用性、技术实现及应用场景的讨论。

不同观点：
• [ruined] 认为镜头的定位和焦点可能是一个问题，由于镜头的螺纹安装通常没有"无限远止动"机制，因此需要手动调整镜头的机械位置以确保正确对焦。他还建议可以通过缩小光圈来增加焦深，类似于眯眼效果。

• [cristoperb] 提出这款设备可以作为现代版CueCat的基础，CueCat是一种早期的条码扫描设备，用于将印刷媒体与互联网内容连接。

• [Ductapemaster] 指出Useful Sensors公司似乎已经转向其他边缘AI技术，不再销售该产品及其人员检测器。

• [harrylepotter] 设想了一种将ESP32条码扫描设备安装在冰箱上的应用，用于跟踪冰箱库存，提升生活便利性。

• [mananaysiempre] 对如何手动实现低技术含量的QR码读取表示疑问，指出常见方案依赖于现成的库（如ZXing和OpenCV），但缺乏对图像处理原理的详细描述。

• [benjaminbenben] 提出将该设备与电子墨水屏结合使用，以实现设备间的消息传递功能。

• [ravetcofx] 提到可以使用ESP32相机模块来实现QR码读取功能，并提供了一个开源项目链接。

• [unquietwiki] 分享了一种车载QR码扫描传感器的设想，用于记录行驶中路过的商家信息，但对其可行性和实用性表示不确定。

• [xmprt] 根据使用经验指出，小型QR码读取器在没有取景器的情况下，使用起来不太方便，缺乏定位和检测反馈。

• [amelius] 寻求一种能够在Linux系统上运行且能读取Digikey包装袋条码的廉价传感器。

• [spicybright] 认为使用便宜的安卓手机可以实现更好的性能和更低的成本。

补充讨论：
- 评论中涉及到的技术问题包括镜头对焦、QR码读取算法、设备应用场景设计等。
- 部分评论者关注该设备的实际应用价值和可行性，如车载QR码扫描、冰箱库存跟踪等创意应用。
- 争议焦点在于是否需要手动实现QR码读取算法以及该设备与其他现成解决方案（如安卓手机）相比的性价比。

data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕追踪彗星和识别星际天体的技术问题及相关讨论。

不同观点：
• [dylan604] 提到在追踪月亮和深空天体时，需要调整EQ mount，并询问哈勃目前的精度及剩余的反应轮数量，质疑高速度天体的追踪难度。
• [rkagerer] 提出一个基础问题，询问在图像中移动的天体是较小的那个（与背景星一起移动）还是较大的那个（相对静止），并对另一个天体的性质表示疑惑。
• [amrrs] 提问如何识别天体为星际彗星，是否通过帧间移动速度判断。
• [throw0101b] 建议通过调整快门速度来减少运动模糊，以改善追踪效果。

补充讨论：
• [hooo] 提到虽然有人猜测该天体可能是外星科技，但更有可能是一个古老的彗星，并提供了一个链接支持其观点。
• 争议焦点之一是如何确认天体为星际彗星，以及高速度天体对现有观测设备（如哈勃）带来的技术挑战。
• 另一个值得注意的讨论点是关于天体在图像中的表现形式（移动与静止）以及如何通过调整设备参数（如快门速度）来优化观测效果。

总结：讨论主要围绕技术性问题展开，包括天体识别方法、观测设备的调整及星际彗星的特性推测。

data.title: Don't animate height
data.author: birdculture
data.article_summary: 本文讲述了作者在开发笔记应用Granola时，发现应用在MacBook上占用60% CPU和25% GPU，最终发现问题源自一个CSS高度动画。作者解释了如何通过Chrome开发工具找到昂贵的动画，以及为何某些动画会如此消耗资源。浏览器渲染CSS动画时，涉及布局、绘制和合成三个步骤，而动画高度会触发布局重算和重绘，是开销最高的属性。相比之下，使用transform和opacity等合成属性开销最小。作者通过将高度动画替换为transform动画，成功解决了性能问题，CPU和GPU使用率大幅下降。文章最后提到下一步将介绍使用Chrome的about://tracing工具进一步优化性能。

不同观点：
• **资源限制与用户选择**：[verall] 提出是否可以限制网页的渲染/绘制时间或资源使用，以防止单一网页消耗过多电池。用户可以选择手动允许某些网页使用更多资源，而非被动接受高资源消耗。该评论强调用户对资源控制的优先权，并质疑网页设计的"艺术性"是否值得消耗如此多资源。

• **GIF与变换技术的性能对比**：[jtangelder] 对简单动画GIF与复合层变换的性能进行比较，提出对不同技术方案性能的疑问。

• **历史性能问题与技术演进**：[Eric_WVGG] 回顾了二十年前高度动画的性能问题，表达了对当前性能问题的惊讶，并分享了自己的技术选择经验。

• **对开发者创新的支持**：[awkward] 支持开发者通过巧妙方法解决问题，认为对音频连接的反馈是有价值的，反对对其工作的批评。

• **自动化编码与性能验证**：[JakeSc] 建议在LLM（大型语言模型）编码时代，浏览器或开发环境应内置性能验证机制，以帮助开发者在开发阶段发现性能问题。

• **定位与合成优化**：[h1fra] 提出将父div设置为绝对定位是否能解决合成问题，表达了对技术方案的疑问。

• **对性能优化的质疑**：[exiguus] 对文章中未展示使用`will-change`和绝对定位的动画性能差异表示质疑，并指出不同浏览器可能存在性能差异。

• **对高资源消耗的批评**：[Varelion] 认为6%的CPU消耗对于一个小动画是过高的，质疑是否有更优化的解决方案。

• **对历史技术与现代技术对比的批评**：[alterom] 将现代网页的资源消耗与数十年前的Flash技术对比，质疑当前网页技术的高资源消耗问题。

• **Canvas的替代方案**：[jasonjmcghee] 建议使用Canvas元素作为替代方案，以优化性能。

补充讨论：
• 评论中多次提到对现代网页技术高资源消耗的质疑，尤其是在对比数十年前的技术时。
• 技术优化建议多样，包括CSS属性、容器技巧、Canvas元素等，反映了开发者在性能优化上的多种思路。
• 用户对资源控制的优先权与技术实现的复杂性是争议的焦点，尤其是在用户体验与性能之间的平衡问题上。

44619206.article_content:
Don't animate height!
Jim Fisher
January 29
Our app was mysteriously using 60% CPU and 25% GPU on my M2 MacBook.
It turned out this was due to a tiny CSS animation!
In this post,
I show how to find expensive animations,
why some are so expensive,
and how to make many animations much cheaper.
Along the way,
we'll learn how the browser renders CSS animations
and how to use Chrome's dev tools for performance profiling.
The problem
While building
Granola
, a note-taking app,
I noticed it was using 60% CPU and 25% GPU on my M2 MacBook:
Activity Monitor showing high CPU and GPU usage
What is Granola spending those cycles on?
It's an Electron app, so let's use the Chrome dev tools to find out!
First, in the "Performance" tab, we see that
most of the time is spent not in JavaScript, but in "rendering" and "painting":
But
what
is it rendering and painting?
To see this, open the "Layers" tab, which shows:
Our window has two layers:
one for the "action bar" at the bottom,
and another for the rest of the document content.
Each layer has a "paint count", and
the action bar's layer is painting every single frame!
Paint flashing (green) and layout shift regions (blue). Dev tools warns
that these animations "may not be suitable for people prone to
photosensitive epilepsy."
Why is the action bar painting so much?
For a clue, jump to the "Rendering" tab,
and turn on "paint flashing" and "layout shift regions".
We quickly see
the browser hates our audio volume visualizer!
Those three green "dancing bars" at the bottom of the Granola window
constantly flash with layout shift and repainting.
But why are the dancing bars causing so much layout calculation?
My first suspicion was DOM updates:
the bars' styles update 10 times per second,
and DOM updates are expensive, right?
But
reducing DOM updates made little difference.
Back to the Performance tab,
and we see this pattern dominating the profile:
That stuff happens once for every frame, 60 times per second.
No JavaScript here — this is pure CSS work!
Why is it doing work every frame?
The answer is in the image.
Look at those three purple "Animation" jobs.
There's one animation job for each dancing bar.
We've found our culprit,
and it's this line of CSS:
transition
:
height
300ms
ease
-
in
-
out
;
Why is this
height
transition so expensive?
What is the browser doing when we animate the
height
property?
We first need to understand
the browser's rendering pipeline.
There are three relevant steps:
Layout
(deciding where elements go on the page), then
Painting
(drawing those elements onto layers like in Photoshop), and finally
Compositing
(merging those layers into a single image).
Here's the browser rendering one frame of Granola:
What happens when we change the
height
property?
It triggers a layout recalculation, followed by re-painting, and re-compositing.
This makes
height
a
layout property
,
and these are the most expensive CSS properties to animate.
The W3C spec is full of these!
Less expensive are
paint properties
.
A paint property does trigger layout,
but it does repaint a layer, and then re-composites.
For example, the
fill
and
stroke
colors on an SVG are paint properties:
they repaint the layer with new colors, then re-composite them.
A funny example is this tiny "bikeshed" SVG
which you can find on
lots of W3C spec pages
.
It costs ~30% CPU!
The cheapest properties are
composite properties
.
They don't trigger layout or paint;
they only trigger a compositing update.
The two classic composite properties are
transform
and
opacity
.
Can we replace our expensive
height
animations with cheaper
transform
animations?
A solution
Naive solution, with warped rounded corners.
A naive solution would be to replace
height
animations with
transform
:
scaleY
(
)
.
And hey presto, this fixes our performance problem!
The "Layout" and "Paint" jobs are nowhere to be seen in the Performance tab.
... Unfortunately, this
scaleY
transform is
ugly
.
Look how those rounded corners get warped as the rectangle stretches!
Instead,
we can create the illusion of a changing height by using
two
rectangles, applying
translate
to each.
There's one rectangle for each end:
The bars are actually pairs of rounded rectangles that move in opposite directions,
creating the illusion of a single stretching bar.
Since we're only using
transform
,
the browser can skip the layout and paint phases.
Here's the optimized version of the visualizer:
Granola audio visualizer, after optimization.
On my M2 MacBook,
the renderer process is now using 6% CPU (down from 15%),
and the GPU process is now using 6% CPU and less than 1% GPU (down from 25% and 20%).
This optimization demonstrates
how understanding the browser's rendering pipeline
and choosing the right CSS properties for animations
can dramatically improve performance.
In the next post,
I'll show how to find hidden performance costs using Chrome's
about
:
//tracing
tool,
which is like the performance profiler on steroids.
See you there!

• **历史性能问题与技术演进**：[Eric_WVGG] 回顾了二十年前高度动画的性能问题，表达了对当前性能问题的惊讶，并分享了自己的技术选择经验。

• **对开发者创新的支持**：[awkward] 支持开发者通过巧妙方法解决问题，认为对音频连接的反馈是有价值的，反对对其工作的批评。

• **自动化编码与性能验证**：[JakeSc] 建议在LLM（大型语言模型）编码时代，浏览器或开发环境应内置性能验证机制，以帮助开发者在开发阶段发现性能问题。

• **定位与合成优化**：[h1fra] 提出将父div设置为绝对定位是否能解决合成问题，表达了对技术方案的疑问。

• **对性能优化的质疑**：[exiguus] 对文章中未展示使用`will-change`和绝对定位的动画性能差异表示质疑，并指出不同浏览器可能存在性能差异。

• **对高资源消耗的批评**：[Varelion] 认为6%的CPU消耗对于一个小动画是过高的，质疑是否有更优化的解决方案。

• **对历史技术与现代技术对比的批评**：[alterom] 将现代网页的资源消耗与数十年前的Flash技术对比，质疑当前网页技术的高资源消耗问题。

• **Canvas的替代方案**：[jasonjmcghee] 建议使用Canvas元素作为替代方案，以优化性能。

补充讨论：
• 评论中多次提到对现代网页技术高资源消耗的质疑，尤其是在对比数十年前的技术时。
• 技术优化建议多样，包括CSS属性、容器技巧、Canvas元素等，反映了开发者在性能优化上的多种思路。
• 用户对资源控制的优先权与技术实现的复杂性是争议的焦点，尤其是在用户体验与性能之间的平衡问题上。

data.title: Go allocation probe
data.author: blenderob
data.article_summary:
本文介绍了作者通过编写一个名为`go_allocation_probe`的工具，分析Go程序中堆分配的具体类型。Go的性能分析工具可以显示分配发生的位置，但不会记录分配的类型。为了解决这个问题，作者利用`bpftrace`和`uprobe`钩取Go运行时中的`mallocgc`函数，捕获每次分配的类型和大小。

Go的每个堆分配都会经过`mallocgc`，通过钩取该函数，作者能够记录分配的类型指针（`TypePtr`）和名称偏移（`NameOff`），以及分配的次数和总大小。然而，`NameOff`只是类型名称的偏移量，需要进一步解析。

作者通过解析Go可执行文件的符号和节区，从`.noptrdata`和`.rodata`节中提取类型名称，最终将偏移量转换为可读的类型名称，从而帮助识别出哪些类型导致了大量内存分配。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Go语言中的内存管理问题、性能分析工具的使用及改进建议

不同观点：
• fsmv认为，在Go中避免将字符串放到堆上非常困难。他使用了内置的逃逸分析工具，并确保在循环中只使用常量内存。然而，他指出，由于接口{}类型会被视为从栈逃逸，传递给fmt函数的字符串会被移到堆上，这是一个主要问题（参见golang/go#8618）。

• felixge强调了使用eBPF分析Go运行时的乐趣，但认为从长远来看，为了提高可靠性和减少开销，建议将此问题作为功能请求提交给Go运行时团队。他建议通过pprof标签在分配分析中提供类型信息。

• jasonthorsness对通过bpftrace工具获取分配信息的方法表示赞赏，并指出通常可以通过观察分配函数来猜测分配的类型，但在涉及大量位置分配的类型（如字符串）时，这种方法尤其有趣。

• osigurdson关注一个具体的代码片段，指出其中的字符串处理部分是值得注意的部分，但没有深入讨论内存管理问题。

• 90s_dev提到了Go团队的一次AMA活动，并询问在那次活动中，AI是否对Go语言的选择产生了影响或提供了建议。

补充讨论：
• 评论中提到了多个工具和方法，如逃逸分析工具、eBPF、pprof标签、bpftrace等，这些工具在分析和解决Go内存管理问题中起到了重要作用。
• 争议的焦点集中在Go语言中字符串分配到堆上的问题，以及是否有必要和如何向Go运行时团队提出改进建议。
• 讨论还涉及对具体代码实现细节的关注，如字符串处理函数的具体操作。
• 另外，提到了AI在Go语言选择中的潜在影响，但未有明确答案。

data.title: Gemini North telescope discovers long-predicted stellar companion of Betelgeuse
data.author: layer8
data.article_summary: 天文学家利用位于夏威夷的北双子望远镜及其搭载的Alopeke仪器，发现了围绕著名红超巨星参宿四（Betelgeuse）的一颗伴星，解开了这颗恒星亮度变化的千年谜团。参宿四是一颗体积巨大且年轻的恒星，其亮度变化曾引发广泛关注，尤其是2019-2020年的“大暗淡”现象，最初被认为可能预示超新星爆发，但后来确认是由于参宿四喷出的尘埃云所致。尽管之前的观测未找到伴星，但通过“斑点成像”技术，研究团队成功直接观测到了这颗距离参宿四很近、质量约为太阳1.5倍的年轻伴星。这一发现揭示了参宿四亮度周期性变化的原因，并展示了高分辨率观测技术的强大能力。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕Betelgeuse伴星的发现及其天文学意义

不同观点：
• [chasil] 引用了关于Betelgeuse伴星的详细信息，指出该伴星质量约为太阳的1.5倍，是一颗年轻的A或B型主序前星，且位于Betelgeuse相对较近的位置，这一发现是首次在红超巨星附近发现如此接近的伴星，并且该伴星在Betelgeuse的外大气层内运行。

• [mkw50505] 对伴星通过引力能量释放发光而非核反应的现象表示惊讶，认为这种现象能被观测到是出乎意料的。

• [e23c16] 对发现的可信度提出质疑，指出检测的统计显著性仅为1.5σ，且图像上存在类似的亮点未被认定为伴星，认为检测声明可能不够充分。

• [dylan604] 提到在Betelgeuse超新星爆发前发现了伴星，并询问是否有伴星在主星超新星爆发后的结果案例。

• [AverageSavage] 以幽默方式提及电影《Beetlejuice》（《阴间大法师》），与天文学主题形成轻松的插曲。

• [pavel_lishin] 猜测伴星是否能解释Betelgeuse亮度变化的现象，并在编辑后确认这一猜测。

• [anjel] 提出一个假设性问题，询问如果一个主序前星被并入一个演化末期（EOL）的恒星，是否会影响后者的时间进程。

• [htrp] 澄清Gemini North是望远镜，而非某种新的AI功能，纠正了对观测设备的误解。

补充讨论：
• [dang] 提到链接的语言版本问题，指出文章常返回西班牙语版本，并采取了替换链接的解决方案。

争议焦点：
• 检测的可信度：[e23c16] 对1.5σ显著性和未被认定为伴星的类似亮点的质疑，与其他评论对发现的接受形成对比。

其他值得注意的讨论点：
• 伴星的发现对Betelgeuse亮度变化的可能解释（[pavel_lishin]）。
• 关于伴星在Betelgeuse超新星爆发后命运的探讨（[dylan604]）。
• 主序前星并入演化末期恒星的影响这一假设性问题（[anjel]）。

44649651.article_content:
Skip to main content
noirlab2523es — Comunicado científico
El telescopio de Gemini Norte descubre compañera estelar de Betelgeuse
El telescopio ubicado en Hawai‘i reveló la nunca antes vista compañera de esta conocida estrella, resolviendo un milenario misterio
21 Julio 2025
×
Un equipo de astrónomos descubrió una estrella compañera girando alrededor de Betelgeuse en una órbita extremadamente estrecha, gracias al instrumento Alopeke de la NASA y de la Fundación Nacional de Ciencias de Estados Unidos, que se encuentra instalado en el telescopio de Gemini Norte en Hawai‘i, la mitad boreal del Observatorio Internacional Gemini, que es financiado en parte por NSF y operado por NOIRLab de NSF. Este descubrimiento responde al milenario misterio de la variación del brillo de la estrella y proporciona información importante sobre los mecanismos físicos que hay detrás de otras estrellas supergigantes rojas variables.
Betelgeuse
es una de las estrellas más brillantes del cielo nocturno y la
supergigante roja
más cercana a la Tierra. Tiene un volúmen enorme, con un radio unas 700 veces mayor que el del Sol. A pesar de tener sólo diez millones de años, lo que se considera joven para los estándares de la astronomía, se encuentra en una fase avanzada de su vida. Situada en el
hombro de la constelación de Orión
, la gente ha observado a Betelgeuse a simple vista por
miles de años
, notando que la estrella cambia de brillo con el tiempo. Los astrónomos establecieron que Betelgeuse tiene un período principal de variación de aproximadamente 400 días y otro período secundario de variabilidad que se extiende a unos seis años.
En 2019 y 2020, se produjo una fuerte disminución del brillo de Betelgeuse —un fenómeno que se conoció como el “Gran oscurecimiento”. Este evento llevó a pensar que se acercaba la muerte de una supernova, pero los científicos pudieron determinar que en realidad se trataba de una
enorme nube de polvo
expulsada por la misma Betelgeuse.
El misterio del Gran Oscurecimiento estaba resuelto, pero el acontecimiento suscitó un renovado interés en el estudio de Betelgeuse, lo que dio lugar a nuevos análisis de datos de archivo sobre la estrella. Uno de estos análisis llevó a los científicos a proponer que la causa de la variabilidad de seis años de Betelgeuse se debía a la presencia de una estrella compañera
[1]
. Pero cuando el
Telescopio Espacial Hubble
y el
Observatorio de rayos X Chandra
buscaron a esta compañera, no se detectó ninguna.
No fue sino hasta que un equipo de astrofísicos liderados por Steve Howell, un investigador científico senior del
Centro de Investigación Ames de la NASA
, que fue posible detectar a la estrella compañera de Betelgeuse, usando un generador de imágenes llamado
‘Alopeke
, que utiliza una técnica conocida como “
speckle imager
”. ‘Alopeke, que en hawaiano significa “zorro”, es financiado por el Programa de Investigación para la Observación de Exoplanetas de NASA–NSF (NN-EXPLORE, por sus siglas en inglés) y se encuentra instalado en el telescopio
Gemini Norte
, la mitad boreal del
Observatorio Internacional Gemini
, financiado en parte por la Fundación Nacional de Ciencias de Estados Unidos y operado por NOIRLab de NSF.
“
Speckle imaging
” es una técnica que se utiliza en astronomía para obtener imágenes utilizando tiempos de exposición muy cortos para congelar las distorsiones en las imágenes causadas por la atmósfera terrestre. Esta técnica logra una alta resolución en las imágenes, la cual, combinada con el poder de recolección de luz del espejo primario de 8,1 metros de diámetro de Gemini Norte, permitió detectar directamente a la tenue compañera de Betelgeuse.
El análisis de la luz de la estrella compañera permitió a Howell y a su equipo determinar sus características. De este modo, descubireron que es seis magnitudes más débil que Betelgeuse en el rango de longitud de onda óptico; tiene una masa estimada de alrededor de 1,5 veces la del Sol y parece se una estrella de
presecuencia principal
de
tipo A o B
, es decir una estrella caliente, joven y de color blanco azulado que aún no ha iniciado la combustión de hidrógeno en su núcleo.
La compañera se encuentra a una distancia relativamente cercana a Betelgeuse, a unas 4 veces la distancia entre la Tierra y el Sol. Este descubrimiento es la primera vez que se detecta una compañera estelar orbitando tan cerca de una estrella supergigante roja. Aún más sorprendente es que la compañera orbita en el interior de la atmósfera exterior de Betelgeuse lo que demuestra la increíble capacidad de resolución de ‘Alopeke.
Luego de comprobar el descubrimiento, Howell destacó
“la capacidad de Gemini Norte para obtener altas resoluciones angulares y contrastes nítidos permitió detectar directamente a la compañera de Betelgeuse,”
. Además, explicó que ‘Alopeke logró lo que ningún otro telescopio pudo hacer antes:
“Los artículos científicos que predijeron la presencia esta compañera estelar, creían que nadie sería capaz de obtener imágenes de ella”

data.author: laserspeed

data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：水印技术的有效性、实现方式及安全性

不同观点：
• Lanedo认为，基于HTML或JS的水印方案较易被移除，有效的方案应将水印嵌入内容本身。他提供了针对图片和音频内容的水印工具示例，并提到HLS分段格式中的水印应用。
• Miki123211支持在HLS分段视频中嵌入水印，认为这种方法能降低计算和带宽成本。他还提出了一种预先编码多个水印变体的算法设想，通过组合爆炸来增强安全性。
• Josephcsible对代码混淆和反调试逻辑持反对态度，认为试图控制他人的计算机是不正当的行为。
• Mlhpdx提出了一种反向思维，即在上传前修改内容以抵消水印效果，从而使水印无法显现。
• Nullbyte指出文章仅讨论了简单的水印技术，而更先进的系统使用神经网络嵌入 invisible watermark（不可见水印），这些水印更难被绕过。
• Laserspeed讨论了绕过水印实施的各种方法，包括Picture-In-Picture技术、客户端保护的错误假设以及通过m3u8播放列表和加密视频段重组视频。
• Mindwipe认为，如果在客户端进行水印处理而没有安全硬件支持，其稳健性难以保证。

补充讨论：
• 水印嵌入位置的有效性问题：Lanedo和Miki123211强调嵌入内容本身的重要性。
• 水印技术的安全性与反制：Josephcsible的道德质疑，Mlhpdx的反向工程设想，Nullbyte对神经网络水印的推崇，以及Laserspeed对绕过技术的详细讨论。
• 实施水印的实际成本和复杂性：Miki123211对HLS分段水印的成本分析和算法设想。
• 对客户端水印处理的信任问题：Mindwipe对安全硬件支持的强调。

data.title: AI Market Clarity
data.author: todsacerdoti
data.article_summary: 本文讨论了人工智能（AI）市场在过去几年中的发展，尤其是生成型AI和基础模型（如大型语言模型，LLM）领域的演变。作者指出，随着OpenAI、Anthropic、Google等公司推出更先进的技术，AI市场的领先者逐渐明晰。在LLM领域，Anthropic、Google、Meta、Microsoft、Mistral、OpenAI和X.AI等公司已成为核心玩家，它们在技术 benchmark 和市场应用上处于领先地位。尽管中国企业如Deepseek、Alibaba Qwen等也推出了具有竞争力的开源模型，但总体上新公司因资本壁垒难以进入这一市场。此外，代码生成等其他AI应用市场也在逐步成熟，但仍存在不确定性。作者总结，尽管当前市场格局逐渐清晰，但未来几年可能会有新的市场和竞争者出现。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：LLM（大型语言模型）在各个领域的应用及其有效性，包括客户服务、法律市场、销售技术以及AI代理的定义和应用。

不同观点：
• bmau5：对LLM在客户服务中的成功表示怀疑，认为当前的AI聊天机器人平台在解决多步骤问题时表现不佳，可能会让用户感到沮丧并放弃使用。
• Dowwie：对Elad作为这些公司的投资者身份提出质疑，认为其观点可能不够中立。
• samtp：希望看到AI代理在实际业务中用于非琐碎问题的具体案例，目前对其应用持怀疑态度。
• chancemehmu：认为AI伴侣市场被严重低估，像Character AI这样的应用在全球范围内非常受欢迎，特别是在年轻人群体中。
• District5524：指出关于AI在法律市场的应用讨论不够全面，推荐了一个更具信息量的报告，并认为某些定制模型的价值不高。
• benreesman：对前端实验室的封闭性表示怀疑，认为中国AI技术发展迅速且具有竞争力，同时对OpenAI等公司的内部运作提出批评。
• panabee：虽然认为LLM相关声明缺乏研究支持，但肯定了文章在调整投资者情绪方面的价值。
• iddan：分享了一个正在开发的AI销售技术项目Closer，展示其实际应用。
• ariwilson：指出产品原型工具如Vercel v0和Firebase Studio在AI驱动开发中的重要性。
• tempusalaria：认为“代理”一词被过度加载，不同公司有不同定义，建议统一使用OpenAI和Anthropic等大实验室的定义。
• benterix：认为文章更像是一个广告，包含大量主观愿望性内容。
• vaenaes：希望看到后AI时代的清晰前景。
• diamond559：指出这些公司成功在于吸引了大量资金，而非来自付费客户。
• boringg：对链接标题表示讽刺。

补充讨论：
• 关于AI在客户服务中的实际效果存在争议，特别是其对用户体验和满意度的影响。
• 对AI在法律和销售领域的实际应用有不同看法，有人认为市场被低估，有人则质疑其价值。
• AI代理的定义混乱，不同公司和研究者有不同的解释，导致沟通和理解上的困难。
• 对中国AI技术发展的速度和竞争力有较高评价，认为其在某些方面可能超过美国公司。
• 对LLM相关投资和市场表现的看法不一，有人认为其成功主要依赖于吸引投资而非实际业务成果。

AI Markets Have Crystalized
AI markets have evolved significantly over the last 4 years. When GPT-3 came out and scaling laws were openly discussed in the AI literature, it seemed clear that you could extrapolate the rate of progress from GPT-2 to GPT-3 onwards through GPT-4, 5 etc and realize a revolution was going to happen.
4 years ago, I started looking for Generative AI companies to back or help start given this curve. I ended up leading or participating in early rounds in companies like
Harvey
,
Perplexity
,
Character.AI
,
BrainTrust
, and others. At the time it was clear to just “back all the best people working on all the biggest problems” because very few people were actually starting generative AI companies. OpenAI seemed to be the only clear foundation model company (with Anthropic pre-launch and promising, Llama non-existent, and Google clearly someone who could (and would eventually) aggressively innovate but was stymied at the time by its own internal processes).
Thanks for reading Elad Blog! Subscribe for free to receive new posts and support my work.
Subscribe
As more people outside of the core AI community woke up to this opportunity, or researchers and engineers from the main labs left to start new companies in AI, the world of AI became murkier. I used to say that
the more I learn about AI, the less I knew about AI
– because it was unclear in many early markets who the likely winners would be and the underlying models and tech were changing so fast. For example in 2022, it was clear code / AI driven software engineering was going to be important, but it was unclear who the winners would be (for example Cursor was not launched until 2023, Codium launched
Windsurf in GA
about 9 months ago, and Cognition launched
Devin
in limited release a bit over a year ago).
We have now entered an era where the first set of AI markets have solidified and a likely set of winners have emerged. This does not mean others won’t show up over time to compete in these markets or that current leaders won’t get acquired or eventually die (just as Stripe launched over a decade after PayPal and 4 or so years after Braintree, and Facebook launched a few years after Friendster and Myspace). We will also see a new set of markets crystalize in the coming few years and these markets today seem quite uncertain.
Markets with more clarity
1. Foundation Models- LLMs
There are many types of foundation models including large language models (LLMs), as well as models for voice, images, video, music, chemistry, biology, materials, physics and other areas.  Foundation models are often driven by scale (of data, compute, certain types of post training and feedback, etc). Scale means capital, so to win in the LLM market you need high availability of capital now entering the many billions.
In the LLM market, a core set of companies have clearly emerged as the ongoing players of the future. They are often partnered with hyperscalers (Amazon with Anthropic, Google GCP with Gemini, Microsoft Azure with OpenAI and its own efforts) as these companies have an economic incentive (cloud spend on AI via AI adoption) to fund these companies that is independent of whether these companies are good investments or not (they often are). Revenue ramps for foundation model companies are rumored to be in the $0 to many $billions range in just 3 or so years, while cloud spend on “AI” has been reported to have reached
a few billion per quarter for some of the main clouds
.
The core players in the LLM world are now Anthropic, Google, Meta (via Llama), Microsoft, Mistral, OpenAI, X.AI. Three or four of these companies are the
clear winners on various benchmarks
and most broadly adopted by developers and enterprise, and are also driving most of the spend in the industry. There are newer entrants like SSI and Thinking Machine Labs driven by brilliant AI researchers, which may either come up with innovative approaches or raise ongoing money to compete, or end up in a few years as acquisitions for companies wishing to enter the market or double down on talent.
In parallel, Chinese companies have launched new open source efforts such as
Deepseek
,
Alibaba Qwen
, and more recently
Kimi
, that perform well on benchmarks. There is a lot to say on Chinese open source LLMs, that might be best covered in a separate post.
In the future, it is unlikely that many new core LLM companies will get started due to capital moats, barring some new breakthrough that somehow doesn’t spread quickly.
Other foundation model markets are still lacking the clear winner or winners although promising companies exist in multiple segments.
2. Code
Co

主要讨论点：个性化折扣模型的数据使用及其在不同地区的合规性

不同观点：
• [kristianc] 指出，由于大多数网站访问者未登录，因此模型在缺乏丰富用户数据的情况下运作。他还强调，这种做法在欧洲可能不符合规定，因为欧洲对用户数据的使用有严格的法律要求（如GDPR）。

• [malshe] 尝试理解模型的运作方式，并询问是否通过用户特征和行为来估计购买概率，并根据该概率决定是否提供折扣。他还进一步询问了决定提供折扣的临界值是否基于数据中的其他变量，暗示模型可能具有复杂的动态机制。

• [klaussilveira] 关注模型如何判断用户不太可能转化。他询问是否使用历史购买数据来进行这种判断，或者是否考虑用户频繁放弃购物车的行为，暗示模型需要多种数据源来提高预测准确性。

• [lazyninja987] 关心商家是否需要向工具提供用户数据以生成个性化折扣，以及除了用户活动数据外，还需要哪些数据来实现最大效果。这表明了对数据隐私和数据需求的关注。

补充讨论：
• 对欧洲市场的合规性是讨论中的一个关键问题，尤其是在用户数据使用方面。
• 模型的技术细节，例如概率估计和临界值的设定，是另一个值得注意的讨论点。
• 数据需求和隐私问题也是用户关注的核心，特别是在涉及个性化折扣生成时所需的数据类型和范围。

争议焦点：
• 主要争议在于数据使用的合法性和隐私问题，特别是在不同司法管辖区（如欧洲）的法律要求下，如何平衡模型有效性和合规性。

• [malshe] 尝试理解模型的运作方式，并询问是否通过用户特征和行为来估计购买概率，并根据该概率决定是否提供折扣。他还进一步询问了决定提供折扣的临界值是否基于数据中的其他变量，暗示模型可能具有复杂的动态机制。

• [klaussilveira] 关注模型如何判断用户不太可能转化。他询问是否使用历史购买数据来进行这种判断，或者是否考虑用户频繁放弃购物车的行为，暗示模型需要多种数据源来提高预测准确性。

• [lazyninja987] 关心商家是否需要向工具提供用户数据以生成个性化折扣，以及除了用户活动数据外，还需要哪些数据来实现最大效果。这表明了对数据隐私和数据需求的关注。

• 数据需求和隐私问题也是用户关注的核心，特别是在涉及个性化折扣生成时所需的数据类型和范围。

• 主要争议在于数据使用的合法性和隐私问题，特别是在不同司法管辖区（如欧洲）的法律要求下，如何平衡模型有效性和合规性。

data.article_summary:
1633年，伽利略因支持地球绕太阳运动的日心说而受到宗教裁判所审判。尽管这一观点并非由他首创，早在古希腊天文学家阿里斯塔克斯就提出过，但在伽利略时代，它遭遇了教会的强烈抵制。这种抵制不仅源于迷信或无知，更因为教会的权力依赖于人们的信仰。教会通过一系列故事、符号和教义构建了叙事主导权，使其权威看似自然且不可动摇。地心说是这一叙事系统的核心，圣经中的某些章节被用来证明地球静止不动，且位于宇宙中心，这不仅体现了人类的特殊地位，也反映了教会所宣扬的神圣社会和精神等级制度。

地心说深刻影响了基督教的生活，包括礼拜仪式、教堂建筑和艺术表现。挑战地心说相当于质疑整个信仰体系，动摇教会对真理的解释权。因此，伽利略的日心说不仅是一个天文学问题，更是对教会权威的根本挑战。

In 1633, Galileo Galilei stood before the Inquisition, not for inventing a radical new theory, but for proposing a straightforward idea: that the Earth moves around the Sun. This wasnât even a new suggestionâGreek astronomers like Aristarchus had floated the heliocentric model centuries earlier. But in Galileoâs time, the idea ran into an insurmountable obstacle.
We often chalk up the Churchâs resistance to superstition or ignorance. While that played a role, there was something deeper at work. The Church wielded immense power, but that power ultimately depended on the beliefs of the people. For society to function as the Church wanted, people needed to carry certain information in their headsâideas that shaped how they behaved, what they valued, and whom they trusted. The Church had mastered the art of narrative dominance, building a system of stories, symbols, and doctrines that made its authority seem natural and inevitable. The geocentric model was one of the cornerstones of this narrative system.
The geocentric model formed a core part of Church doctrine and daily life. For example, Psalm 104:1-6 (KJV) reads:
Bless the Lord, O my soul. O Lord my God, thou art very great; thou art clothed with honour and majesty. Who coverest thyself with light as with a garment: who stretchest out the heavens like a curtain: Who layeth the beams of his chambers in the waters: who maketh the clouds his chariot: who walketh upon the wings of the wind: Who maketh his angels spirits; his ministers a flaming fire:
Who laid the foundations of the earth, that it should not be removed for ever.
Thou coveredst it with the deep as with a garment: the waters stood above the mountains.
Likewise, Joshua 10:12-13 (KJV) describes:
Then spake Joshua to the Lord in the day when the Lord delivered up the Amorites before the children of Israel, and he said in the sight of Israel, Sun, stand thou still upon Gibeon; and thou, Moon, in the valley of Ajalon.
And the sun stood still, and the moon stayed,
until the people had avenged themselves upon their enemies. Is not this written in the book of Jasher? So the sun stood still in the midst of heaven, and hasted not to go down about a whole day.
These passages were cited as literal proof that the Earth was stationary and central. This cosmic arrangement justified humanityâs special status: sermons and theological writings argued that God placed humans at the center of the universe, making them the focus of divine attention and salvation. The structure of the cosmosâEarth at the center, surrounded by concentric spheres of planets, stars, and heavenâmirrored the Churchâs vision of a divinely ordained social and spiritual hierarchy.
You could see this worldview in action throughout Christian life. The Churchâs liturgical calendarâincluding the calculation of Easterârelied on the apparent movements of the Sun and Moon around a stationary Earth. Cathedrals like San Petronio in Bologna were equipped with meridian lines and astronomical clocks, turning the very architecture into solar observatories for tracking the heavens as seen from Earthâs center. In art, illuminated manuscripts and stained glass windows depicted the universe as a series of concentric spheres, with Earth at the heart of creation. The rose windows of Gothic cathedrals, with their radiating spokes, visually echoed the cosmic order, while creation scenes in church art often showed God setting the Sun, Moon, and stars in motion around a central Earth.
Miracles described in the Bible, like the Sun standing still for Joshua, made sense only in a geocentric universe. Even the moral orderâthe idea that the corrupt Earth was surrounded by the pure heavensâdepended on this model. Accepting heliocentrism would have meant unraveling a whole tapestry of beliefs, not just about the stars, but about God, humanity, and the Churchâs place in the world.
The Churchâs worldview was a bonafide conceptual cathedral. Its visible rituals and teachings rested on a hidden architecture of interlocking ideas, each supporting and reinforcing the others. At the very foundation was the belief that Christianityâand specifically the Churchâwas the sole authority on interpreting reality. The geocentric model was a crucial supporting pillar: it was drawn directly from scripture and literally carved into the intellectual and physical fabric of Christian society. To question geocentrism was to question the explanatory power of scripture itself, and by extension, the Churchâs authority to define what was true.

We can visualize this kind of belief system as a graphâa network of concepts, values, and connections. When you challenge a core idea, youâre not just questioning a single point; youâre tugging at the beams and arches of the entire cathedral.

data.title: Show HN: Any-LLM – Lightweight router to access any LLM Provider
data.author: AMeckes
data.article_summary:
**any-llm** 是由 Mozilla AI 开发的一个开源项目，旨在通过单一接口与不同的语言模型（LLM）提供商进行通信。它提供了简单统一的接口，使用一个函数即可与所有支持的提供商交互，并通过字符串切换模型。该项目具有以下特点：

1. **开发者友好**：提供完整的类型提示和明确的错误信息。
2. **利用官方SDK**：确保兼容性并减少维护负担。
3. **框架无关**：适用于各种项目和用例。
4. **无需代理或网关服务器**：简化设置过程。

项目解决了LLM接口标准化和现有解决方案的局限性问题，支持多种LLM提供商，并提供了Python 3.11及以上版本的安装和使用指南。

[项目链接](mozilla-ai.github.io/any-llm/)

• 核心争议在于是否需要重新实现LLM接口。swyx认为这是必要的，而amanda99则认为LiteLLM的实现存在实际问题。
• 另一个争议点是关于LiteLLM项目的成熟度和文档质量，amanda99指出了其不足之处。

• 关于使用代理和跨语言支持的需求和优势，不同参与者提出了各自的看法和建议。

any-llm
A single interface to use and evaluate different llm providers.
Documentation
Supported Providers
Key Features
any-llm
offers:
Simple, unified interface
- one function for all providers, switch models with just a string change
Developer friendly
- full type hints for better IDE support and clear, actionable error messages
Leverages official provider SDKs
when available, reducing maintenance burden and ensuring compatibility
Stays framework-agnostic
so it can be used across different projects and use cases
Actively maintained
- we use this in our own product (
any-agent
) ensuring continued support
No Proxy or Gateway server required
so you don't need to deal with setting up any other service to talk to whichever LLM provider you need.
Motivation
The landscape of LLM provider interfaces presents a fragmented ecosystem with several challenges that
any-llm
aims to address:
The Challenge with API Standardization:
While the OpenAI API has become the de facto standard for LLM provider interfaces, providers implement slight variations. Some providers are fully OpenAI-compatible, while others may have different parameter names, response formats, or feature sets. This creates a need for light wrappers that can gracefully handle these differences while maintaining a consistent interface.
Existing Solutions and Their Limitations:
LiteLLM
: While popular, it reimplements provider interfaces rather than leveraging official SDKs, which can lead to compatibility issues and unexpected behavior modifications
AISuite
: Offers a clean, modular approach but lacks active maintenance, comprehensive testing, and modern Python typing standards.
Framework-specific solutions
: Some agent frameworks either depend on LiteLLM or implement their own provider integrations, creating fragmentation
Proxy Only Solutions
: solutions like
OpenRouter
and
Portkey
require a hosted proxy to serve as the interface between your code and the LLM provider.
Quickstart
Requirements
Python 3.11 or newer
API_KEYS to access to whichever LLM you choose to use.
Installation
In your pip install, include the
supported providers
that you plan on using, or use the
all
option if you want to install support for all
any-llm
supported providers.
pip install
'
any-llm-sdk[mistral,ollama]
'
Make sure you have the appropriate API key environment variable set for your provider. Alternatively,
you could use the
api_key
parameter when making a completion call instead of setting an environment variable.
export
MISTRAL_API_KEY=
"
YOUR_KEY_HERE
"
#
or OPENAI_API_KEY, etc
Basic Usage
The provider_id key of the model should be specified according the
provider ids supported by any-llm
.
The
model_id
portion is passed directly to the provider internals: to understand what model ids are available for a provider,
you will need to refer to the provider documentation.
from
any_llm
import
completion
import
os
# Make sure you have the appropriate environment variable set
assert
os
.
environ
.
get
(
'MISTRAL_API_KEY'
)
# Basic completion
response
=
completion
(
model
=
"mistral/mistral-small-latest"
,
# <provider_id>/<model_id>

=

"role"
:

,

44650567.article_summary:
**any-llm** 是由 Mozilla AI 开发的一个开源项目，旨在通过单一接口与不同的语言模型（LLM）提供商进行通信。它提供了简单统一的接口，使用一个函数即可与所有支持的提供商交互，并通过字符串切换模型。该项目具有以下特点：

1. **开发者友好**：提供完整的类型提示和明确的错误信息。
2. **利用官方SDK**：确保兼容性并减少维护负担。
3. **框架无关**：适用于各种项目和用例。
4. **无需代理或网关服务器**：简化设置过程。

项目解决了LLM接口标准化和现有解决方案的局限性问题，支持多种LLM提供商，并提供了Python 3.11及以上版本的安装和使用指南。

[项目链接](mozilla-ai.github.io/any-llm/)

data.title: Reverse Proxy Deep Dive: Why HTTP Parsing at the Edge Is Harder Than It Looks
data.author: miggy
data.article_summary:
本文深入探讨了反向代理中的HTTP处理复杂性。主要内容包括：

1. **HTTP处理流程**：从接收请求、解析和清理请求，到选择上游主机、转发请求和响应，每一步都可能面临性能和安全挑战。
2. **HTTP协议演变**：从HTTP/0.9到HTTP/2，协议的不断演变增加了处理的复杂性，要求系统持续更新。
3. **不同组件的生命周期差异**：客户端、代理和服务器可能使用不同的语言和框架，代理需管理它们之间的兼容性。
4. **性能考虑**：请求大小和类型的多样性要求代理具备灵活的配置和处理逻辑，以平衡内存消耗和吞吐量。
5. **缺乏行业标准**：URL长度、Cookie大小等限制在不同平台上差异显著，导致不一致性。
6. **安全问题**：代理作为第一道防线，需防御恶意攻击，确保系统安全。

这些问题使HTTP处理在反向代理中变得复杂，需要灵活配置和持续更新以应对各种挑战。

44647600.article_content:
In
Part 1
of this series, we explored a high-level overview of reverse proxies and dived deep into connection management. This post shifts our focus to the intricate world of HTTP handling within a reverse proxy.
Deep Dive into HTTP Handling
At a high level, the HTTP workflow from a proxy’s perspective might seem straightforward:
Receive the request from the client
Parse and sanitize the request
Uses different requst metadata (path, headers, cookies) to select an upstream host
Manipulates the requests as needed
Send the request to the selected upstream
Read the response from the upstream
Sanitize the response
Forward response to the client
While many standard libraries support these steps, making them work reliably at scale, and meeting strict security and compliance requirements, is surprisingly complex. From malformed requests and malicious attacks to browser quirks, this layer becomes a battleground for performance, correctness, and resilience.
What Makes It Complex
Challenges in HTTP parsing
The Evolution of the HTTP Protocol
Over the years, http spec has significantly evolved. It started with simple request lines like GET /index.html in
HTTP/0.9
, moved to newline-separated headers and persistent connections in
HTTP/1.1
, and later adopted full binary framing and multiplexing in
HTTP/2
.
Each new version brought added features, redefined earlier assumptions, and introduced additional complexity. These changes require continual updates to existing systems, libraries, and tooling.
MDN offers a detailed exploration of
HTTP’s evolution
for those interested in a deeper dive.
Different Development Lifecycles of Clients, Proxies, and Servers
Clients and servers are often developed using different languages, frameworks, and platforms, each with their own independent lifecycles. Some systems, like in-car music players, may remain in use for 15 years or more, while clients and proxies evolve more rapidly. This disparity places the responsibility on the proxy layer to act as an intermediary, managing compatibility between components. The proxy often must decide which parts of the RFC specifications to enforce strictly and where to allow flexibility.
Examples include:
According to the HTTP/1.1 specification, header names are case-insensitive. However, some clients and servers expect header names in a specific case. Reverse proxies typically provide a way to preserve or normalize casing. For instance, Haproxy provides a
case option
for preserving case and Envoy provides similar
functionality
.
HAProxy has an option to accept invalid requests using
accept-unsafe-violations-in-http
.
Performance Considerations: One Size Doesn’t Fit All
Not all requests are the same. Some are small, while others carry large payloads. Some include long URLs or large cookies, while others do not. These variations make it difficult for proxy developers to create a single, highly efficient logic that works well in all cases. As a result, proxies often need to provide flexible configuration options and write code that can adapt to different traffic profiles.
These profiles can sometimes be in conflict. For example, supporting large header sizes requires more memory to parse and process incoming requests. At high throughput, this leads to increased memory usage and can affect overall system performance. This creates a trade-off between request size, memory consumption, and throughput.
Lack of Industry-Wide Standards for Key Limits
Limits like maximum URL length, cookie size, and header size vary widely across platforms, and in some cases, the default settings provided by frameworks or servers are surprisingly low or outdated.
Azure Front Door imposes the following
limits
on URL and query size:
Maximum URL size — 8,192 bytes — Specifies maximum length of the raw URL
(
scheme +
hostname
+ port + path + query string of the URL
)
Maximum Query String size — 4,096 bytes — Specifies the maximum length of
the query string,
in
bytes.
Maximum HTTP response header size from health probe URL — 4,096 bytes —
Specified the maximum length of all the response headers of health probes.
Past investigations into cookie size reveal similar inconsistencies
Google Chrome — 4096 bytes
Internet Explorer — 5117 bytes
Firefox — 4097 bytes
Microsoft Edge — 4097 bytes
Typically, the following are allowed:
300 cookies
in
total
4096 bytes per cookie
20 cookies per domain
81920 bytes per domain
Handling quotes in Set-Cookie headers, whether single, double, or escaped, adds another layer of confusion. Some libraries interpret them strictly, others ignore them, and a few may even fail altogether. This inconsistency often leads to subtle bugs or broken behavior across browsers and frameworks. Here’s a great read on the challenges of
cookie handling
and how it impacts major websites.

data.title: Blip: Peer-to-peer massive file sharing
data.author: miles
data.article_summary: Blip是一款文件传输应用，能够直接发送文件，无需分开上传和下载，且无大小限制。它支持断点续传，即使网络中断或设备问题也不会影响传输进度。Blip具备轻量级应用、不耗电、跨设备传输、全球发送、保持文件高质量、以及TLS 1.3加密等特点。相比WeTransfer、Dropbox和Aspera等服务，Blip无需存储文件到云端，传输速度更快，操作更简便，且完全免费用于非商业用途。与AirDrop等本地分享工具不同，Blip不受设备距离限制，适合大文件的跨设备传输。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Blip文件传输工具的特性、技术实现及其替代方案

不同观点：
• [Blip创始团队观点]  
Blip的创建是为了解决在互联网上向其他设备或人发送高质量照片、视频和大文件的难题。其目标是保持界面简洁，但底层技术强大，支持P2P传输、直接连接以及中继备选方案，并优化了大型媒体传输，具备E2EE加密和无数据货币化，通过捐赠和订阅模式盈利。

• [Saris的疑问]  
Saris质疑Blip声称的P2P传输模式，因为在提到“互联网发送在高峰期可能较慢”的同时，Blip又声称传输速度可以达到连接的最大速度，这似乎存在矛盾。Saris推测这可能与NAT中继连接有关。

• [ryandotsmith的技术推测]  
ryandotsmith对Blip的技术实现感到好奇，猜测可能使用了QUIC协议和中继服务器，或类似于Tailscale的DERP技术。

• [rahimnathwani的替代方案]  
rahimnathwani分享了自己在Android和iOS设备间传输文件的解决方案，使用Wormhole William和Destiny，但指出了配置和传输过程中的不便之处。

• [packetlost的开源偏好]  
packetlost表示如果Blip是开源的会更愿意使用，暗示对闭源软件的不信任。

• [poisonborz的替代方案]  
poisonborz推荐了免费开源的替代工具PairDrop。

• [miksak的市场观察]  
miksak质疑文件共享工具在非技术用户中的广泛适用性，因为大多数非技术用户已经习惯使用云服务存储和共享数据。

• [satvikpendem的技术好奇]  
satvikpendem对Blip的技术栈表示好奇，并提到了另一个使用P2P库Iroh的工具Sendme。

• [leosanchez的平台需求]  
leosanchez对Blip的Android应用表示赞赏，但期待Linux版本的发布。

• [abcd_f的语义挑剔]  
abcd_f对Blip描述中的“超高速”用词提出批评，认为这种表达不准确。

• [manoji的推荐]  
manoji推荐Syncthing作为稳定的同步工具，并称赞Blip的用户体验。

• [timc3的API问题]  
timc3指出Blip未提及是否提供API。

• [greener_grass的类比]  
greener_grass将Blip比作跨平台的AirDrop。

• [system2的实用性质疑]  
system2质疑Blip的必要性，认为大多数云服务已经足够管理大文件，对Blip的新颖性表示怀疑。

• [supportengineer的类比]  
supportengineer认为Blip类似于YouSendIt。

补充讨论：
• 关于Blip是否开源的讨论，部分用户对闭源软件持保留态度，并提出了开源替代方案。
• 对Blip技术实现的猜测和讨论，包括使用的协议和中继方案。
• 用户对跨平台文件传输工具的需求和现有替代方案的分享。
• 对Blip在非技术用户中市场适用性的质疑。

data.title: CSS's problems are Tailwind's problems
data.author: coltonv
data.article_summary: 文章批评Tailwind将CSS和现代网页开发的所有缺点集中在一起，是一种倒退。文章首先回顾了CSS的成功与失败，指出CSS在样式应用方面提供了内联样式和样式表两种有效方式，尽管存在一些问题，如样式覆盖和调试困难。CSS与JavaScript的分离既是优势也是劣势，导致变量共享和样式一致性成为挑战。现代工具如styled-components和vanilla-extract尝试解决这些问题，但各有局限。Tailwind被批评为通过类的方式强制使用内联样式，将样式信息隐藏在字符串中，导致可读性和调试难度增加，且无法利用样式表的强大功能。文章认为Tailwind加剧了CSS原有的问题，并将其应用到不必要的地方。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Tailwind CSS的优缺点以及其在现代web开发中的应用

不同观点：
• **lenkite的观点**：Tailwind的CSS声明在复杂设计下会变得非常冗长，导致可读性和维护性差。他举例说明了一个简单的按钮需要大量类名，导致眼疲劳和头痛。他认为Tailwind在接手他人项目时尤其难维护。

• **wwweston的观点**：Tailwind通过要求开发者设置配置文件来统一样式常量，这对大项目和多开发者协作非常有利。他认为Tailwind使代码更易读和维护，尤其是对经验不足的开发者而言。

• **exiguus的观点**：Tailwind可以与CSS模块、SASS等工具结合使用，并且可以通过组件库和自定义组件来减少重复代码。他强调了通过组件化来实现DRY原则的重要性。

• **hbn的观点**：基于多年使用Tailwind和Angular的经验，他认为Tailwind在跨项目维护和大团队协作中表现出色，尤其在样式一致性和减少代码交叉引用方面。

• **freddydumont的观点**：他认为Tailwind在模板系统中有优势，但在React组件中不如CSS-in-JS，因为后者提供了样式封装。他还提到了使用无运行时的CSS工具，如vanilla-extract或PandaCSS。

• **iambateman的观点**：Tailwind结合AI使用效果显著，并且相比Bootstrap等其他框架更优。他认为Tailwind用户有权选择自己喜欢的工具，而不应被反对者干扰。

• **tptacek的观点**：质疑文章中对Tailwind的批评，认为其成功不仅因为配置文件，还因为大量前端团队的采用，应给予更多认可。

• **wuz的观点**：Tailwind的生态系统依赖大量额外工具使其可用，且代码可读性差。他认为Tailwind不是好的解决方案，只是当前生态系统中其他选项更差。

• **ipsento606的观点**：在使用nativewind过程中感到需要掌握多种技术，体验糟糕，唯一的好处是全局样式常量的统一。

• **hombre_fatal的观点**：对Tailwind的批评多源于其表面的类名冗长，但其细粒度的一致性类和死码消除特性在构建第三方组件库时具有优势。

• **theSherwood的观点**：Tailwind的优势包括样式与标记共存、避免样式继承问题和合理的默认设置，但需要构建步骤和配置。他认为CSS-in-JS是更差的解决方案。

• **ARandomerDude的观点**：推荐使用tailwind-merge解决类名顺序和重复业务逻辑问题。

• **ahuth的观点**：Tailwind的流行是因为它能明确知道应用了哪些样式，特别是在多开发者环境下，尽管类名行很长很丑。

• **jbreckmckye的观点**：作为传统CSS和BEM的用户，他对Tailwind的优点感到困惑，想了解其主要好处。

• **CreepGin的观点**：Tailwind在提供支持和共享代码片段时非常方便，可以减少额外CSS文件或行内样式，但在非浏览器环境中的支持较差。

补充讨论：
• Tailwind的配置文件和全局样式常量被认为是其重要优势之一，特别是在大团队和多项目中。
• Tailwind在复杂设计下的类名冗长和可读性差是被广泛提及的缺点。
• 不同开发者对Tailwind与CSS-in-JS、Bootstrap等其他解决方案的比较有不同看法，各有偏好。
• AI在结合Tailwind使用中的潜力被提及，认为可以提高生产力。
• 争议焦点在于Tailwind的可读性和维护性，特别是在接手他人项目时的体验。

44649036.article_content:
Tailwind is the Worst of All Worlds
21 July 2025
React
,
CSS
,
Tailwind
,
HTML
Tailwind is the worst of all worlds. It is a regrettable step backwards that takes everything bad about CSS and modern web development and brings it all together in one library.
CSS's Successes and Failures
Of all the web technologies that underlie the modern web, the one that has received the fewest fundamental changes is CSS. We've gotten amazing things like flexbox, grid, container queries, and more which have supercharged the ability to quickly build responsive styles. While we're far from the days of using tables for layout and googling "how to vertically center css" once a week, the language semantics themselves hasn't had to change much. This is because CSS offers two well rounded ways of applying styles that work pretty well: inline styles and stylesheets.
Inline styles let you quickly add targeted rules to a single element. Much maligned historically due to the fact that many abused them and thus failed to keep their code DRY, there's really nothing wrong with inline styles. If there
is
something wrong with them, it's simply that an HTML attribute is a kind of clunky place to write out styles. They'll wander off screen on your editor once you have enough rules and it's harder to get nice formatting or static analysis. But if you're a good developer you won't use inline styles this way very often. (This is what we call foreshadowing).
Stylesheets are the much more powerful feature. They let you assign a set of rules to zero, one, or many elements at once with the minimum amount of code. They also include all the fancy features like media queries, container queries, and pseudo-elements, which are not available inline. Flaws that existed in the early days of stylesheets have largely been remedied, albeit not always in the most desirable way. SCSS variables had broader support (since they simply compiled to basic CSS) and were prettier than CSS variables, but eventually SCSS started losing steam in the face of an improving CSS.
CSS definitely isn't perfect. Like JavaScript's
==
operator, some ideas were bad then and are still bad now. CSS chooses which styles overwrite others based on selector specificity, leading some style debugging to be a bit of a rat's nest where the developer ends up bailing out to
!important
tags, which just kick the can down the road. Worse yet, when two rules have the same specificity, the default functionality is to pick whichever is defined last in the
stylesheet
. So, in this example, the styles of
two
win out over
one
, because the
.two
rule is declared after the
.one
rule, even though the
one
class comes second on the div.
<
style
>
.one
{
text
:
red
}
.two
{
text
:
blue
}
</
style
>
<
div
class
=
"
two one
"
>
</
div
>
With modern multi-sheet websites and bundlers, this can get confusing fast as it can be hard to keep track of which sheet was loaded first on every page.
Additionally, CSS's status as a separate language from JavaScript is a blessing and a curse. It's a blessing in that CSS can be downloaded, parsed, and rendered in parallel extremely quickly by modern browsers, sidestepping the single-threadedness of JavaScript. But a curse in that modern apps simply require some amount of JavaScript-CSS interop since CSS is not a general purpose language. Sharing variables to keep styles consistent betweent he two means duplicating code between the two languages.
Much of these problems are solved with modern tooling, albeit often with their own caveats. Tools like
styled-components
brought JS and CSS together fairly seamlessly, giving you all the power of JavaScript (functions, etc) in your CSS. The caveat is that styles are compiled into Javascript (slow, single threaded) rather than CSS (fast, parallel). Tools like
vanilla-extract
have done an admirable job giving you fully typed CSS-in-JS-in-CSS, compiling JS created styles into CSS files. Lastly, tools like React have made inline styling much better with objects that are linter, type system, and formatter friendly.
Okay, now can we dunk on Tailwind?
For reasons we'll get into later, Tailwind decided to burst on to the scene and become the default styling solution for all modern web development despite taking each and every one of these problems, exacerbating them, and applying them to places that didn't have them before. Lets see how Tailwind replicates CSS's main paradigms. Remember, inline styles let you control single element styles simply and fairly explicitly:
style="background: red; color: blue;"
. Classes let you control multi-element styles simply, with the slight annoyance that it's easy to misspell your class name and spend way too long debugging before realizing it:
class="todo-item"
.
Tailwind exclusively offers inline styles via classes. Classes are single strings separated by spaces, not key-value pairs. So the classes must be something like
class="bg-red txt-blue"
. Key and value must be obscured into a plain string, lowerin

data.title: From Cartography to Code: Architectures of Power at the Venice Biennale 2025
data.author: bryanrasmussen
data.article_summary: 在第19届威尼斯建筑双年展上，Kate Crawford教授和Vladan Joler教授的装置作品《Calculating Empires: A Genealogy of Technology and Power Since 1500》荣获银狮奖。该作品通过单色地图形式，呈现了过去五百年间帝国、殖民主义、军事化和技术权力的历史结构，揭示了当代技术政治背后的权力架构。作品跨越两面平行墙，垂直代表时间，水平展示控制、通信、计算和分类系统，观众可以按世纪、主题或图案自行导航，探索从海底电缆到卫星网络、殖民地图到预测算法的联系。作品批判了视觉化政治，强调图表和地图并非中立，而是塑造知识和权力的工具。通过慢读和反思，作品邀请观众重新思考推动当今所谓“进步”的历史和权力结构。Crawford和Joler强调，图表作为政治干预的形式，揭示了技术和权力的复杂关系。

From Cartography to Code: Architectures of Power at the Venice Biennale 2025
STIR speaks to Kate Crawford and Vladan Joler on their Silver Lion-winning 'large scale visual manifesto' traversing history, colonialism, militarisation and technology.
by
Ayesha Adonais
Published on : Jul 19, 2025
At the 19th edition of the
Venice Architecture Biennale
, curated by
Carlo Ratti
under the theme
Intelligens: Natural. Artificial. Collective
, the Silver Lion for promising participation was awarded to
Calculating Empires: A Genealogy of Technology and Power Since 1500
– an urgent, masterfully researched and executed data visualisation by Prof. Kate Crawford, a leading scholar of the social and political impacts of
artificial intelligence
, and Prof. Vladan Joler, an academic and artist whose work blends data investigations, critical cartography and data visualisation. Housed in the Arsenale, this provocative monochromatic cartography unfolds like a networked cosmos, mapping five centuries of imperial and technological power. Built not of stone or steel, but of symbols, systems and structures of control, its spatial logic forms a visual genealogy that frames empire as both political force and technological condition.
Exhibition view of
Calculating Empires
at the 19th International Architecture Exhibition, La Biennale di Venezia
Image: Marco Cappelletti; Courtesy of La Biennale di Venezia
Spanning two parallel walls,
Calculating Empires
traces evolving architectures of power. Time runs vertically; systems of control, communication, computation and classification extend horizontally. It visualises the historical structures that underpin contemporary technopolitics, revealing how
infrastructures
enclose not only time and territory, but thought itself. Visitors self-navigate by century, theme or motif, tracing connections from submarine cables to satellite networks, colonial cartographies to predictive algorithms, encountering a work that continually evolves, its meaning shifting with each act of reading and positionality.
The work interrogates the politics of
visualisation
, revealing how flowcharts, Gantt charts, neural networks and logic gates, far from neutral, shape how knowledge is produced and power, organised. By appropriating these forms, Crawford and Joler turn diagrammatic language into both critique and methodology. In a world of speed and simplification,
Calculating Empires
resists the bite-sized logic of platforms and elicits a deliberate act of slow reading that insists on friction, opacity and reflection. Its symbolic and historical references demand context, time and thought. In the age of algorithmic governance, it invites us to reconsider whose histories power the systems we now call progress.
Calculating Empires
was awarded the Silver Lion for promising participation at the 19th International Architecture Exhibition, La Biennale di Venezia
Image: Marco Cappelletti; Courtesy of La Biennale di Venezia
The display glacially traces technological patterns of colonialism, militarisation, automation and enclosure since 1500
Image: Luca Capuano; Courtesy of  La Biennale di Venezia
In conversation with STIR, we discussed the politics of
mapping
, the aesthetics of control and why slowing down and re-seeing is more urgent than ever.
Ayesha Adonais: You describe this work as a ‘visual genealogy’. Why did you choose the diagrammatic form, and what did it allow you to reveal that other formats might not have?
Kate Crawford:
Every one of those diagrams is doing a form of ideological work. One of the things that has been core to the way Vladan and I have worked together for eight-plus years is thinking about the politics of diagrams – as a political form and a type of political intervention. Our earlier work,
Anatomy of an AI System
, mapped the single Amazon Echo and the planetary scale of extraction in space. That was really spatial [in nature]. We realised we always wanted to do a temporal version, a diagram about time. Really expanding the idea of a simple timeline to create a deep, diagrammatic mapping of politics and power, constructed in the form of a diagram, which we see as inherently political.
Vladan Joler:
My obsession with that form developed over the last 15 years. It began with a small investigation of a single internet packet, which gradually grew in complexity, evolving into large-scale infrastructures, data flows and power relations. I fell in love with the form because it offers possibilities that other forms do not; it’s a non-linear structure that allows people to explore, read and engage. There is no
cartography
without the cryptographic bias of the person creating it. I struggled with creating a space that isn’t 100 per cent accurate; it can’t be, because you'r
